In-scope systems.value: SERFF Industry - Filing Rules and Filing Access for the review-method lookup and prior-approval search; determinations recorded in the filing determination log

checklist.step: Open a determination worksheet for the approved Accident product change
actions: Open the product change queue and filter Product Line = Accident and Status = 'Approved for filing determination'.

Copy onto a new determination worksheet: product name, writing company and NAIC company code, TOI H03 Accident Only, target effective date, jurisdiction list (all 51 or a named subset) and new-business-only vs new plus in-force.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the hard date driver (statutory mandate, distribution commitment, release train) and record it on the worksheet header.
Attach the signed change request and save the folder as ACC-<company>-H03-<target effective date>.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries product, writing company, TOI, target effective date and jurisdiction list, with the signed change request attached.

checklist.step: Decompose the change into filable elements and tag every row
actions: List every artifact the Accident change touches on its own worksheet row - base policy form, endorsement, rider, application, enrollment form, mandated notice, outline of coverage, marketing piece.
Tag each row FORM, RATE, RULE or NON-FILED; outline of coverage and application are FORM rows in most jurisdictions even when the base policy is unchanged.
Hand the RATE rows to the Product / Filing Actuary for the per-state rate level impact and record the figure returned in writing.
Flag any row that changes benefit triggers, exclusions or the definition of covered accident - those never qualify as non-filed.
checklist.done: every touched artifact has a tagged row and rate rows carry a written rate level impact from the actuary.

checklist.step: Capture form numbers and edition dates exactly as printed
actions: Open each draft Accident form in the document repository and read the form number and edition date from the footer of page 1 and the last page.
Type the form number and edition into the worksheet row character for character, including suffixes such as -AK for state variants.
Compare each number against the approved-forms inventory to confirm it is either a new number or a genuine new edition of an existing number.
Reject any draft whose footer is missing, watermarked DRAFT, or inconsistent between pages, and return it to Product Development the same day.
checklist.done: every form row shows the exact printed form number and edition date and no draft-marked artifact remains in scope.

checklist.step: Read Alaska's current SERFF filing rules for TOI H03 Accident Only
actions: Log in to SERFF with the company instance and open Industry - Filing Rules, then select Alaska.
Set Business Type = Life, Accident and Health and drill to TOI H03 Accident Only and the matching Sub-TOI.
Read the Alaska General Instructions and open the attached Accident and Health form filing requirements checklist and any referenced Division bulletin.
Note the review requirement (prior approval with a 30-day review window and possible extension under the Alaska form-filing statute) and the fee schedule shown on the state's SERFF page.
Print the instructions to PDF as AK-filing-rules-H03-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it in the determination folder as the evidence behind the Alaska call.
checklist.done: a dated Alaska filing-rules capture and requirements checklist for TOI H03 sit in the determination folder.

checklist.step: Repeat the filing-rules capture across the remaining 50 jurisdictions
actions: Work the jurisdiction list in SERFF Filing Rules state by state, including the District of Columbia, and capture each state's H03 General Instructions to PDF with the capture date in the filename.
Record for each state the review method, the stated review period in days, the fee amount and payment method, and whether the state demands its own transmittal or certification form.

Pull the same TOI entry from the NAIC Product Requirements Locator for Arizona, California and Connecticut and reconcile it to the SERFF instructions, since those three jurisdictions carry named supporting citations for this obligation.
Where instructions are silent or contradictory, email the state's SERFF contact listed on the state page and log the question, the date sent and the answer on the worksheet row.
checklist.done: all 51 jurisdictions have a dated rules capture and a recorded review method, review period, fee and transmittal requirement.

checklist.step: Test whether the Accident forms fall inside the IIPRC uniform standards route
actions: Check the IIPRC uniform standards index for the product type: the Compact covers individual and group life, annuity, disability income and long-term care, so accident-only forms normally sit outside it.
Where a rider on the Accident policy is a disability income or long-term care benefit, record that the rider may be Compact-eligible while the base accident form is not.

Record the conclusion on the worksheet header - 'Compact-eligible: no, accident-only base form; state-by-state filing required in all 51 jurisdictions' - with the standards page reference and date read.
Confirm with Regulatory Counsel before routing any element to the Compact, since a Compact filing removes the state-level route for that element.
checklist.done: the worksheet states whether each element is Compact-eligible, with the standards reference and date, and counsel has cleared any Compact routing.

checklist.step: Confirm the product coding against the NAIC uniform coding matrix
actions: Open the NAIC Uniform Life, Accident and Health Product Coding Matrix and locate TOI H03 Accident Only and the Sub-TOI that matches the benefit design (for example accident-only, accidental death and dismemberment, or accident medical expense).
Confirm each state's SERFF Filing Rules page lists that TOI and Sub-TOI as accepted through SERFF for the writing company's licence type.
Where a jurisdiction takes the product outside SERFF, record the alternate channel - state portal URL or paper filing address - and capture its own instructions.
Write the TOI, Sub-TOI, filing type and submission channel onto every state row on the worksheet.
checklist.done: TOI, Sub-TOI, filing type and channel are recorded for every jurisdiction and agree with the coding matrix.

checklist.step: Set the review method for every state and element pairing
actions: Set each state/element row to PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE, INFORMATIONAL / FILE-FOR-RECORD or EXEMPT.

Paste into the row the exact sentence from the state's General Instructions that drove the call, plus the statutory or bulletin citation (Alaska AS 21.42.120 on the representative row; the Arizona, California and Connecticut form-filing statutes on their rows).
Highlight every prior-approval jurisdiction - those set the critical path for the Accident launch date.
Have a second Regulatory Filing Specialist re-read the ten largest-premium jurisdictions and initial the rows.
checklist.done: every state and element row carries a review method, a quoted source sentence, a citation and a peer initial on the ten largest jurisdictions.

checklist.step: Search SERFF Filing Access for an approval that already covers the form edition
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access and search by NAIC company code, state, TOI H03 and the form number.
Filter Disposition to Approved / Filed / Closed-Approved and sort by disposition date descending.
Open the closest match, download the approved form attachment and compare it page for page to the new edition, paying attention to benefit definitions, exclusions and the schedule page.
Claim reuse only where the approved text is identical for that jurisdiction; copy the SERFF Tracking Number and disposition date onto the worksheet row.
checklist.done: each row states either reuse with a SERFF tracking number based on an inspected prior filing, or new filing required.

checklist.step: Name a specific exemption for every 'no filing required' call
actions: For each EXEMPT or NON-FILED row, name the basis: previously approved edition unchanged, group certificate issued out of a filed situs policy, employer-sponsored exempt group class, advertising material outside the form-filing statute, or internal procedure.
Paste the statute, regulation or bulletin citation that grants the exemption with its effective date.
Where the exemption depends on a threshold such as group size or eligible group class, record the tested value and the source of that value.
Never leave a row reading only 'not required' - an unsupported row is treated as filing required.
checklist.done: every exempt row carries a named basis, a citation and any tested threshold value.

checklist.step: Compute the deemer clock and the latest submission date per jurisdiction
actions: Record the review period from each state's instructions or statute on the row - Alaska 30 days from receipt with a possible 30-day extension; other jurisdictions commonly 30, 45 or 60 days.
Add internal lead times: package preparation days, actuarial and legal review days, and a 10-business-day objection-response buffer.
Compute latest submission date = target effective date minus (review period + extension allowance + objection buffer + implementation lead) and write it on the row.
Load each latest submission date into the filing calendar and set T-120/T-90/T-60/T-30 reminders against the Accident target effective date.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction row shows the review period, the computed latest submission date and a calendar entry with reminders.

checklist.step: Confirm the writing company is licensed for the line in each jurisdiction
actions: Pull the certificate of authority record for the writing company and list the lines of authority granted in each of the 51 jurisdictions.
Confirm accident and health authority exists in every jurisdiction on the filing list; a filing cannot cure a missing licence.
Where authority is absent or restricted, remove the jurisdiction from the launch scope and notify the Insurance Product Manager in writing the same day.
Record the licence status, line of authority and verification date on each jurisdiction row.
checklist.done: each jurisdiction row shows verified accident and health authority for the writing company, or the jurisdiction is removed from scope.

checklist.step: Write the determination rows into the Filing Determination Log
actions: Add one log row per jurisdiction per element with: change id, jurisdiction, form number and edition, element type, filing required Y/N, review method, filing type, citation, review period days, latest submission date, reuse tracking number, decider and decision date.
Link every row to the determination folder holding the dated filing-rules captures.
Set status to 'Determined - pending counsel' on exempt and prior-approval rows, and 'Determined - closed' on the rest.
Run the log's blank-field validation report and clear every hit before handing over.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per jurisdiction per element with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the exempt and prior-approval calls
actions: Route to counsel every 'no filing required' row and every prior-approval jurisdiction row, with the dated rules capture attached.
Counsel re-reads the cited statute or bulletin as it reads on the determination date and confirms or overturns the call in writing on the row.
Overturned rows return to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for rework within the same week and are re-routed for sign-off.
Confirmed rows are stamped with counsel name and date and moved to 'Determined - closed'.
checklist.done: no exempt or prior-approval row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation on the row.

checklist.step: Publish the determination and arm the pre-use release gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the Accident product change record and circulate it to Product Operations, Pricing and IT.
Set the release gate flag on every prior-approval jurisdiction: no Accident form may be issued there until an approval letter or a satisfied review period is recorded against the row.
Give the implementation team the per-jurisdiction earliest-use dates so policy admin availability rules are dated accordingly.

Where a latest submission date is already unreachable, escalate to the Head of Compliance within one business day with three written options - move the effective date, drop the jurisdiction, or launch on the previously approved edition.
checklist.done: the change record shows a per-jurisdiction earliest-use date, prior-approval jurisdictions are gated, and any unreachable date has a written owned decision.

testing.step: Build the population of Accident form changes that went live in the quarter
actions: Extract from the policy administration change log every Accident form, endorsement, rider and application change with an effective date inside the quarter, by writing company and jurisdiction.
Add forms-repository publications and document-template releases so a template swapped without a policy admin change cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract row count to the quarter's release notes and to the forms inventory delta, and clear every difference before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and record the extract date and query used.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to release records and the forms inventory and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every implemented Accident form to a determination that pre-dates it
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on change id plus jurisdiction plus form number and edition.
Confirm the determination decision date is earlier than the form's effective date in that jurisdiction.
List unmatched rows and determinations dated on or after the effective date as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Quantify the exposure on each unmatched row - policies issued on that form in that jurisdiction since the effective date.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception with an issued-policy count.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of rows in prior-approval jurisdictions and 100% of Alaska rows as the representative jurisdiction for this obligation.
Take 25 further rows by seeded random selection from the remainder, with a minimum total sample of 40 rows.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection tool in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Include every element type at least once - base form, endorsement, rider and application.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all prior-approval and Alaska rows and every element type.

testing.step: Re-perform the review-method call in SERFF for each sampled row
actions: Open SERFF Industry - Filing Rules for the sampled jurisdiction and TOI H03 Accident Only and read the General Instructions as they stood at the determination date.
Reach an independent review-method conclusion before opening the determination worksheet.
Compare to the recorded method; a difference is an exception, including a correct method supported by the wrong citation.
Screenshot the instructions page relied on into the workpaper with the date of capture.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent re-performance note and a captured source page.

testing.step: Verify the TOI coding and submission channel on the sample
actions: Look the product up in the NAIC Uniform Life, Accident and Health Product Coding Matrix and compare TOI and Sub-TOI to the determination row.
Confirm the recorded submission channel matches what the jurisdiction's SERFF page accepts for that TOI and licence type.
Flag miscoded rows for root-cause work, since a wrong TOI means the wrong General Instructions were read and the review method is unreliable.
Re-test the review method on any miscoded row using the corrected TOI.
testing.done: TOI, Sub-TOI and channel agree with the coding matrix on every sampled row, or the difference is logged and re-tested.

testing.step: Test the support behind every 'no filing required' call in the sample
actions: Pull each exempt row and read the cited statute, regulation or bulletin as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the exemption covers the specific element claimed under it, including any group-size or eligible-group threshold and the tested value recorded.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists and pre-dates the jurisdiction's go-live date.
Treat an uncited 'not required' as a failed control, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every exempt row is supported by a verified citation, any tested threshold and a dated counsel sign-off that pre-dates go-live.

testing.step: Trace every 'filing required' row to a real SERFF submission
actions: In SERFF Filing Access search the SERFF Tracking Number recorded on the sampled row.
Confirm the filing exists for the correct writing company, jurisdiction, TOI H03 and form number and edition date.
Read the submission date and disposition and compare both to the form's effective date in that jurisdiction.
Where reuse of a prior approval was claimed, open the prior filing and confirm the approved edition is the edition in use today.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every filing-required row traces to a real SERFF filing for the right company, jurisdiction and form edition.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer arithmetic and prove the pre-use gate held
actions: For all sampled prior-approval rows, recompute latest submission date = effective date minus (review period + extension allowance + objection buffer + implementation lead) using the state's stated review period.
Compare the actual submission date to the recomputed date and note every filing submitted after it.

Confirm the policy admin availability date for the jurisdiction is on or after the approval date or the satisfied review-period date - for Alaska, at least 30 days after the Division's receipt date with no disapproval.
Treat any Accident policy issued before approval or a satisfied review period as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled jurisdiction issued Accident coverage before approval or a satisfied review period, and the deemer arithmetic reconciles.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying change id, jurisdiction, form number and edition, what was missed and the policies exposed.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - change not intaken, wrong TOI, stale instructions, licence gap, timeline compressed - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for use-before-approval breaches, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel covering the affected jurisdiction.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the population and compare it to the zero-unfiled-form threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer who authored none of the sampled determinations sign the workpaper.
Report the results and any open pre-use breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-001.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Pull each jurisdiction's Accident form filing requirements checklist
actions: In SERFF open Industry - Filing Rules, select the jurisdiction and TOI H03 Accident Only, and download the state's form filing requirements checklist and required supporting-documentation list.

Transcribe every mandatory item into the package matrix as its own row - cover letter, transmittal, redline, Statement of Variability, readability certification, actuarial memorandum, outline of coverage, third-party authorization, fee.
Mark each row Required / Conditional / Not applicable and record the condition text verbatim where it is conditional.
Save the downloaded checklist as <state>-H03-checklist-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf in the filing folder.
checklist.done: the package matrix holds a dated, per-jurisdiction row list drawn from the current state checklists.

checklist.step: Assemble the final Accident form set as filing-grade PDFs
actions: Request print-ready PDFs from Product Development with the form number and edition date printed on every page and John Doe sample data in variable fields.
Open each PDF and confirm it is text-searchable, free of DRAFT watermarks and comment markup, and within the SERFF attachment size limit of roughly 3 MB per attachment.
Confirm state-variant forms carry the state suffix in the form number and that the variant text matches the state's mandated language.
Name each file <form number>_<edition>_<state>.pdf and lock the version in the repository so the as-filed copy cannot be edited later.
checklist.done: a locked, filing-grade PDF exists for every form in scope, correctly named and within attachment limits.

checklist.step: Produce the redline against the currently approved edition
actions: Retrieve the approved prior edition from the filing archive using the SERFF tracking number on the determination row.
Generate a side-by-side or marked-up comparison showing every insertion and deletion, including schedule pages and exclusions.
Write a short change narrative per change: what changed, why, and whether it is benefit-enhancing, benefit-reducing or neutral for the insured.
Where the form is brand new, state 'new form, no prior edition' and attach the approved companion form it will be issued with.
checklist.done: each revised form has a redline plus a per-change narrative, and new forms are labelled as such.

checklist.step: Obtain the readability (Flesch) certification
actions: Run the Flesch Reading Ease score on the full policy text excluding the schedule, medical terms and defined terms as each state's readability statute permits.
Confirm the score clears the jurisdiction's minimum - commonly 40 for accident and health forms, higher in a handful of states named on their checklists.
Where the score falls short, return the form to Product Development with the sentences driving the score rather than re-running the calculation with different exclusions.
Prepare the signed readability certification naming form number, edition, score and the exclusions applied, one per jurisdiction that requires it.
checklist.done: a signed readability certification exists for every form and jurisdiction that requires one, with a score above the state minimum.

checklist.step: Build the Statement of Variability for all bracketed material
actions: List every bracketed or variable item in the Accident forms - benefit amounts, elimination periods, issue ages, company address, officer signatures, optional benefit blocks.
For each item state the permitted range or the fixed set of alternatives and the circumstances under which each is used.
Add the standard undertaking that variability will be administered in a non-discriminatory manner and that any use outside the stated range will be refiled.
Cross-check that no bracket in the PDF is missing from the Statement, and no Statement row references a bracket that no longer exists.
checklist.done: every bracket in the filed PDFs maps to a Statement of Variability row with a stated range and use condition.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial memorandum and rate exhibits for the Accident benefits
actions: Document the benefit description, pricing assumptions (morbidity basis, lapse, expense, interest), issue-age and benefit-amount ranges and the rating structure.
Show the anticipated lifetime loss ratio by jurisdiction and demonstrate it meets each state's minimum loss ratio standard for individual accident and health business.
Attach rate tables and sample rate calculations at representative issue ages and benefit amounts so the reviewer can reproduce a premium.
Sign the actuarial certification as a qualified actuary under the US Qualification Standards and date it.
checklist.done: a signed, dated actuarial memorandum with loss ratio demonstration, rate tables and reproducible sample calculations exists.

checklist.step: Confirm every state-mandated notice and endorsement is in the package
actions: Work each jurisdiction's checklist for mandated content - fraud warning wording, free-look period length, guaranty association notice, grievance and appeal language, mandated definitions of covered accident.
Compare the mandated wording character for character against the form text and record the page and paragraph where each requirement is met.
Where a requirement is met by a separate notice rather than the base form, add that notice to the package as its own form row.
List unmet requirements for Product Development with the checklist citation attached rather than filing and hoping.
checklist.done: each mandated content requirement maps to a page and paragraph of a filed document, with no unmet items outstanding.

checklist.step: Write the cover letter and filing description
actions: Open with the writing company name, NAIC company code, TOI H03 Accident Only and Sub-TOI, and the requested effective date.
State what is being filed, what it replaces (with prior SERFF tracking numbers and approval dates), and whether it applies to new business only or also in force.
Summarise the change narrative from the redline in plain language and identify anything benefit-reducing up front.
Name the filing contact with direct phone and email, and confirm the filer is authorised to act for the company in that jurisdiction.
checklist.done: the cover letter names company, TOI, prior filings replaced, the substance of the change and an authorised contact.

checklist.step: Complete the NAIC uniform transmittal and any state-specific transmittal
actions: Fill the Uniform Transmittal Document with company details, TOI and Sub-TOI, filing type, form numbers and editions and the requested effective dates.
Complete the Form Filing Attachment listing each form number, edition, form name, form type and replaced form.
Add any state-specific transmittal or certification that the jurisdiction's checklist names, completing the certification statements exactly as worded.
Have a second reviewer compare the transmittal form list to the PDF file list before it is signed.
checklist.done: the transmittal set is complete, signed and its form list agrees item for item with the PDFs in the package.

checklist.step: Clear third-party filer authorisation where a vendor files on the company's behalf
actions: Confirm whether a third-party filer will submit in any jurisdiction and, if so, retrieve the current authorisation letter on company letterhead.
Check the letter names the writing company, the NAIC company code, the jurisdictions covered and an expiry date that runs past the expected disposition date.
Where the letter has expired or omits a jurisdiction, obtain a re-executed letter signed by an officer before submission.
File the authorisation letter into the filing folder and add it to the package matrix as a required item for those jurisdictions.
checklist.done: a current, in-scope authorisation letter exists for every jurisdiction where a third-party filer will submit.

checklist.step: Compute the filing fee for each jurisdiction and arrange payment
actions: Read the fee from each jurisdiction's SERFF filing rules page - typically a per-form or per-filing amount for accident and health form filings.
Multiply by the number of forms or filings as the state's fee rule requires and record the computed amount on the package matrix row.
Confirm the accepted payment method for the jurisdiction - SERFF EFT, state portal payment or paper cheque - and pre-authorise the EFT account balance with Finance Operations.
Where a fee is paid outside SERFF, obtain the payment reference so it can be attached to the submission.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction has a computed fee, a confirmed payment method and funds or a payment reference in place.

checklist.step: Run the internal QC pass against the state checklist
actions: Walk the package matrix row by row for the jurisdiction and tick each Required item against the actual file in the package folder.
Open each PDF and confirm the form number, edition date and page count match the transmittal and the Statement of Variability.
Reject the package back to the assembler where any Required row is unmet - a package is never submitted with a placeholder.
Sign and date the QC checklist and store it in the filing folder.
checklist.done: a signed QC checklist shows every Required item matched to a named file for that jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Obtain legal review and sign-off before submission
actions: Review the redline, the cover letter and any benefit-reducing change for consistency with the jurisdiction's statute and mandated wording.
Review and approve in writing any deviation from a state checklist item, including any bypass explanation to be entered in SERFF supporting documentation.
Confirm the certification statements on the transmittal are accurate before an officer signs them.
Record the sign-off with counsel name and date on the filing tracker row.
checklist.done: counsel has signed the package and approved in writing every deviation and bypass explanation.

checklist.step: Freeze the package and produce the manifest
actions: Lock the filing folder to read-only and produce a manifest listing every file with its name, size, page count and checksum.
Record the manifest against the filing tracker row so the as-filed set can be proved later against what SERFF holds.
Copy the frozen package into the SERFF staging area under the jurisdiction and TOI.
Any post-freeze change starts a new version of the package with a new manifest - the frozen version is never edited.
checklist.done: the package is read-only, manifested with checksums and staged for submission.

checklist.step: Hand the package to the filing analyst with the deadline context
actions: Update the tracker row to 'Package complete' with the manifest reference, QC checklist and counsel sign-off attached.
Restate the latest submission date and the target effective date from the determination so the analyst knows the buffer remaining.
Flag the prior-approval jurisdictions and any jurisdiction with a long historical review time for priority submission.
Confirm the handover in writing to the Regulatory Filing Specialist who will submit.
checklist.done: the analyst holds a complete package, the latest submission date and a written handover on the tracker row.

testing.step: Build the population of Accident packages submitted in the quarter
actions: Extract from the filing tracker every TOI H03 filing with a submission date inside the quarter, with jurisdiction, SERFF tracking number, form numbers and editions.
Cross-check the count to the SERFF workspace filing list for the same date range to catch filings submitted without a tracker row.
Record the extract date, filter criteria and row count and have the extractor sign completeness.
Resolve every difference between tracker and SERFF before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the SERFF workspace filing list and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the manifest of each package to what SERFF actually holds
actions: Open the SERFF filing and list the attachments on the Form Schedule, Rate/Rule Schedule and Supporting Documentation tabs.
Compare that list to the frozen package manifest file by file, including page counts.
Note any attachment present in SERFF but absent from the manifest, or vice versa, as a control break in package freezing.
Confirm the attached form PDFs carry the same edition dates as the transmittal.
testing.done: SERFF attachments and the frozen manifest agree file for file, or every difference is logged.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record its selection
actions: Take 100% of packages filed in prior-approval jurisdictions and the Alaska package as the representative jurisdiction.
Take 15 further packages by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 25 packages in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool in the workpaper.
Include at least one package that drew an objection and one that was approved without objection.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers prior-approval jurisdictions and includes both objected and clean filings.

testing.step: Re-perform the checklist completeness test against the state's own requirements
actions: Download the jurisdiction's current Accident and Health form filing requirements checklist from SERFF Filing Rules for TOI H03.
Tick each Required item against the SERFF attachments independently, without reading the internal QC checklist first.
Compare the independent result to the signed QC checklist and treat any Required item marked complete internally but absent in SERFF as a fail.
Screenshot the state checklist page used into the workpaper with its capture date.
testing.done: each sampled package has an independent completeness conclusion supported by a captured state checklist.

testing.step: Recompute the readability score and re-test the certification
actions: Re-run the Flesch Reading Ease calculation on the as-filed policy text for five sampled forms using the exclusions the certification claims.
Compare the recomputed score to the certified score and to the jurisdiction's minimum.
Confirm the certification names the correct form number and edition and is signed and dated before the submission date.
Flag any certification where the exclusions applied are broader than the statute permits.
testing.done: recomputed readability scores agree with the certifications and clear the state minimums, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test the Statement of Variability against the filed forms
actions: For each sampled package, list every bracketed item in the as-filed PDFs by page.
Match each bracket to a Statement of Variability row with a stated range or alternative set.
Flag brackets with no Statement row and Statement rows with no bracket, both of which draw objections.
Compare the ranges stated to the ranges actually configured in the policy administration system for that jurisdiction.
testing.done: every filed bracket maps to a Statement row whose stated range matches the configured range, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify the actuarial memorandum is signed, qualified and self-consistent
actions: Confirm the memorandum carries a dated signature and qualification statement from a credentialed actuary and pre-dates the submission date.
Re-perform two sample premium calculations from the filed rate tables and compare to the memorandum's worked examples.
Recompute the anticipated lifetime loss ratio from the filed assumptions and compare it to the state minimum cited.
Flag any memorandum whose benefit description does not match the as-filed form text.
testing.done: sample premiums and the loss ratio reproduce from the filed exhibits and the certification is validly signed and dated.

testing.step: Test fees, transmittals and filer authorisation
actions: Recompute the filing fee from the jurisdiction's published fee rule and the form count actually filed, and compare to the amount paid in SERFF.
Confirm the transmittal form list agrees item for item with the Form Schedule rows in SERFF.
Where a third-party filer submitted, confirm an unexpired authorisation letter covering that jurisdiction was on file at the submission date.
Log underpaid fees separately - they stall dispositions and can void a file-and-use date.
testing.done: fees recompute to what was paid, transmittals agree with the Form Schedule and filer authorisations were current at submission.

testing.step: Root-cause the objections raised against sampled packages
actions: Read each objection letter on the sampled filings and classify it as package defect, substantive product issue or state interpretation.
For package defects, name the matrix row that should have caught it and raise a tracker issue to update the companion-item matrix.
Compute the package-defect objection rate across the population and compare it to the 10% rebuild trigger.
Assign an owner and remediation date to each matrix update.
testing.done: every objection is classified, package defects have owned matrix updates and the defect rate is computed against the trigger.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the package test
actions: Summarise fails by category - missing required item, readability, variability, actuarial, fee, authorisation - with counts and the affected jurisdictions.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer who assembled none of the sampled packages sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-001 and report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with categorised fails, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Create the SERFF filing shell for the jurisdiction
actions: In SERFF select Create New Filing, choose the writing company instance and the jurisdiction from the determination row.
Set Business Type = Life, Accident and Health, TOI = H03 Accident Only and the Sub-TOI matching the benefit design.
Set Filing Type to the review method recorded in the determination - Form, Form and Rate, or Informational.
Enter a Company Tracking Number in the house convention ACC-H03-<state>-<yyyy>-<sequence> so tracker and SERFF can be reconciled later.
checklist.done: a filing shell exists with the correct company, jurisdiction, TOI, Sub-TOI, filing type and house tracking number.

checklist.step: Complete the General Information tab
actions: Enter the filing description summarising the Accident forms filed, what they replace and whether they apply to new business only.
Enter the requested effective dates for new business and renewal business exactly as agreed in the determination.

Answer the domicile questions - status of the filing in the state of domicile, and whether the filing was approved, pending or not required there - and attach the domicile approval if the state asks for it.
Answer the market type, group type and overall rate impact questions; leave nothing at a default the state will object to.
checklist.done: General Information carries a substantive description, requested effective dates and completed domicile and market answers.

checklist.step: Complete the Company and Contact tab and confirm the filing contact
actions: Select the writing company and confirm the NAIC company code, FEIN, state licence number and domicile shown match the corporate record.
Set the filing contact to the named analyst with direct phone and monitored email so objection letters reach a person, not a shared box.
Where a third-party filer submits, record the authorised filer details and attach the authorisation letter.
Correct any stale company data with Corporate Legal before submitting rather than filing under an outdated record.
checklist.done: company data matches the corporate record and a reachable named filing contact is recorded.

checklist.step: Populate the Form Schedule with every form being filed
actions: Add one Form Schedule row per form with form number, edition date, form name, form type (policy, certificate, application, endorsement, outline of coverage) and action (new, revised, replaced).
On revised or replaced rows enter the previous filing's SERFF tracking number and the form number and edition being superseded.
Attach the locked filing-grade PDF to its row and open the attachment in SERFF to confirm it rendered correctly.
Reconcile the row list to the package manifest and the transmittal before moving on.
checklist.done: every form has a Form Schedule row with the correct action, prior filing reference and a rendered attachment.

checklist.step: Populate the Rate/Rule Schedule where the filing carries rates
actions: Add a Rate/Rule Schedule row per exhibit with document name, affected form numbers, rate action (new, revised) and previous state filing number.
Enter the rate information fields the jurisdiction requires - overall percentage rate impact, written premium change, policyholders affected and maximum and minimum percentage change.
Attach the rate tables and rating manual pages in the format the state's instructions demand, spreadsheet where required rather than PDF only.
Reconcile the overall rate impact entered to the figure in the actuarial memorandum before submission.
checklist.done: each rate exhibit has a schedule row with rate impact figures that reconcile to the actuarial memorandum.

checklist.step: Satisfy every Supporting Documentation item the state requires
actions: Open the Supporting Documentation tab and work each required item the state has configured - cover letter, transmittal, redline, Statement of Variability, readability certification, actuarial memorandum, certifications.
Attach the corresponding file from the frozen package to each item and check the file name matches the manifest.
Where an item genuinely does not apply, enter a bypass explanation naming the reason and the checklist condition rather than attaching an empty file.
Confirm Regulatory Counsel has approved each bypass explanation before it is entered.
checklist.done: every required supporting-documentation item is satisfied by an attachment or a counsel-approved bypass explanation.

checklist.step: Compute and pay the filing fee inside SERFF
actions: Open the Filing Fees section and compare the amount SERFF calculates to the fee computed from the state's published fee rule during package assembly.
Where SERFF requires manual entry, enter the computed amount and the fee explanation showing the per-form arithmetic.
Select EFT and confirm with Finance Operations that the SERFF EFT account is funded for the batch of filings going out that week.
Where the state takes payment outside SERFF, attach the payment reference or cheque copy to supporting documentation.
checklist.done: the fee shown in SERFF matches the independently computed fee and a funded payment method is attached.

checklist.step: Run the SERFF validation and submit the filing to the state
actions: Run the SERFF validation check and clear every error and warning; do not submit over a warning without a written note explaining it.
Have a second Regulatory Filing Specialist review the filing on screen against the QC checklist for prior-approval jurisdictions before submission.
Submit the filing and capture the SERFF Tracking Number, the submission date and time and the state's receipt confirmation.
Download the submission confirmation to the filing folder as the proof of the pre-use filing date.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted with zero unresolved validation errors and the tracking number and dated confirmation are filed.

checklist.step: Handle jurisdictions that take Accident forms outside SERFF
actions: For any jurisdiction flagged in the determination as an alternate channel, follow the state portal or paper instructions captured with the determination.
Submit through the state portal or by courier with tracked delivery, and obtain a stamped or electronic receipt showing the state's receipt date.
Record the state's own file number, receipt date and reviewer contact in the filing tracker in place of a SERFF tracking number.
Scan the receipt into the filing folder so the review clock start date is provable.
checklist.done: every non-SERFF jurisdiction has a dated receipt, a state file number and a tracker row equivalent to a SERFF row.

checklist.step: Open the tracker row with the review clock and deemer date
actions: Create or update the tracker row with SERFF tracking number, company tracking number, jurisdiction, form numbers and editions and submission date.
Enter the state's review period from the determination and compute the deemer date - for Alaska, 30 days from the Division's receipt date, extendable by a further 30 days on notice.
Set the alerts at deemer minus 10 days and on the deemer date, and a 15-day recurring nudge while status is Pending State Action.
Set the row status to Submitted and link it to the frozen package manifest.
checklist.done: the tracker row shows submission date, review period, computed deemer date and armed alerts.

checklist.step: Sweep SERFF status daily and mirror changes into the tracker
actions: Each business day open the SERFF workspace filing list filtered to open Accident filings and read the status column and message centre.
Record every status change - Assigned, Pending State Action, Objection Letter issued, Amendment required - onto the tracker row with the date it appeared.
Route any Objection Letter to the objection-response process the same day it is seen.
Escalate any filing whose status has not moved for 15 days beyond the state's stated review period to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every open filing has a status read within the last business day and every status change is mirrored to the tracker.

checklist.step: Follow up filings that pass the state's review period without action
actions: Produce the weekly aging report of Accident filings open beyond the state's stated review period, sorted by days over.
For each, send a status enquiry through the SERFF message centre naming the tracking number, submission date and the statutory review period, and log the date sent.
Where the jurisdiction operates a deemer, confirm with Regulatory Counsel in writing whether the deemer has run before any reliance is placed on it.
Escalate filings more than 30 days over the review period to the Head of Compliance with the launch impact stated.
checklist.done: every over-age filing has a logged enquiry, a counsel position on any deemer, and an escalation where more than 30 days over.

checklist.step: Capture the disposition and download the state's decision documents
actions: When the state closes the filing, open the Disposition tab and read the disposition status - Approved, Filed, Acknowledged, Disapproved, Withdrawn or Closed.
Download the disposition report and the approval letter or state correspondence and file them in the filing folder.
Read the disposition for conditions - approved as amended, approved for new business only, approved with a stated effective date - and record the condition verbatim on the tracker row.
Record the disposition date, which is the date from which the forms may be used in that jurisdiction unless the letter says otherwise.
checklist.done: the disposition status, date, any conditions and the downloaded approval letter are recorded against the tracker row.

checklist.step: Confirm the approved editions are the editions the company will issue
actions: Open the disposition's attached form list and compare each approved form number and edition date to the frozen package manifest.
Where the filing was approved as amended, download the amended PDF from SERFF and make that the controlled edition in the forms inventory.
Retire the superseded edition in the forms inventory with the disposition date as its end date.
Escalate any mismatch between what was approved and what the implementation team holds before configuration begins.
checklist.done: the approved edition of every form is identified, controlled in the forms inventory and matched to what implementation will use.

checklist.step: Publish disposition status to Product Operations and close the filing row
actions: Update the tracker row to Approved or Filed with the disposition date, conditions and the earliest-use date for the jurisdiction.
Notify Product Operations and the Insurance Product Manager so the release gate for that jurisdiction can be opened against documented evidence.
Issue the weekly filing status report to product governance showing submitted, pending, objected, approved and disapproved counts by jurisdiction.
Move disapproved or withdrawn filings into the refiling workflow with a Compliance Manager sign-off on the plan.
checklist.done: the tracker shows a closed row with an earliest-use date, Product Operations has been notified and the weekly report has been issued.

testing.step: Build the population of Accident filings submitted or dispositioned in the quarter
actions: Export from the SERFF workspace every TOI H03 filing for the writing companies with a submission or disposition date inside the quarter.
Export the equivalent rows from the filing tracker and add non-SERFF jurisdictions filed through state portals.
Reconcile the two lists on tracking number and list every SERFF filing with no tracker row and every tracker row with no SERFF filing.
Sign the reconciled population as complete with the export date and filter criteria recorded.
testing.done: the SERFF export and the tracker reconcile row for row and the population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Test submission timeliness against the determined latest submission date
actions: Join each population row to its Filing Determination Log row and read the latest submission date computed there.
Compare the actual SERFF submission date to that date and compute days early or late for every row.
List every late submission as an exception and record whether the target effective date was then missed or the launch proceeded on a prior edition.
Summarise the days-early distribution by jurisdiction to show whether the objection buffer is being preserved.
testing.done: days early or late is computed for every filing and every late submission is listed as an exception with its launch consequence.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the selection
actions: Take 100% of filings in prior-approval jurisdictions, 100% of Alaska filings, and 100% of filings that were disapproved or withdrawn.
Take 20 further filings by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 35 in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool in the workpaper.
Include at least three non-SERFF channel filings if the population contains any.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers prior-approval, Alaska, adverse-disposition and alternate-channel filings.

testing.step: Re-perform the SERFF schedule population check on the sample
actions: Open each sampled SERFF filing and read the Form Schedule rows - form number, edition, form type, action and prior filing reference.
Compare each row to the frozen package manifest and the transmittal and flag any form filed with the wrong edition date or a missing replaced-form reference.
Confirm every Supporting Documentation item is satisfied by an attachment or a bypass explanation and that each bypass carries a counsel approval.
Capture the Form Schedule screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing's schedules and supporting documentation are independently verified against the manifest and captured.

testing.step: Recompute the review clock and deemer date for each sampled filing
actions: Read the state's stated review period from its current SERFF General Instructions and the underlying statute as at the submission date.
Recompute the deemer date from the state's receipt date shown in SERFF - for Alaska, receipt date plus 30 days, plus any noticed 30-day extension.
Compare the recomputed date to the deemer date recorded on the tracker row and flag differences.
Where reliance was placed on a deemer, confirm the file shows no disapproval or extension notice before that date.
testing.done: recomputed deemer dates agree with the tracker, and every deemer relied upon is supported by an absence of state action on file.

testing.step: Trace each sampled disposition to the state's own decision document
actions: Open the Disposition tab and download the disposition report and approval letter for each sampled filing.
Compare the disposition status, date and any conditions to what the tracker records, character for character on conditions.
Confirm the approved form numbers and editions in the disposition match the forms in the company's controlled forms inventory.
Flag any tracker row showing Approved where the state document says approved as amended, approved with conditions, or acknowledged only.
testing.done: every sampled disposition traces to a downloaded state document whose status, date, conditions and form editions match the tracker.

testing.step: Test disposition capture latency
actions: For each sampled filing compare the SERFF disposition date to the date the tracker row was updated.
Compute the latency in business days and compare to the 2-business-day standard.
List every breach and check whether the delay held up the release gate for that jurisdiction.
Summarise median and worst-case latency by analyst to show where the daily sweep is failing.
testing.done: capture latency is computed for every sampled filing and every breach of the 2-day standard is listed with its gate impact.

testing.step: Age the open filings and test the follow-up discipline
actions: List every Accident filing still open at quarter end with days since submission and days beyond the state's stated review period.
For each filing over the review period, look for a logged status enquiry in the SERFF message centre and check its date.
Flag over-age filings with no enquiry, and filings more than 30 days over with no escalation to the Head of Compliance.
Quantify the launch exposure - jurisdictions still gated because of an open filing.
testing.done: every over-age filing is listed with its enquiry and escalation status and the gated-jurisdiction exposure is quantified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying jurisdiction, SERFF tracking number, form editions and what failed.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - late package, validation warning overridden, wrong edition attached, missed status sweep, unfunded fee, no follow-up on an over-age filing - and an owner.
Set a remediation date; for disapproved filings, require a refiling plan signed by the Compliance Manager.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, for disapprovals, a signed refiling plan.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the submission and disposition test
actions: Compute the late-submission rate, the disposition capture latency breach rate and the over-age follow-up failure rate against the population.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, with the workpaper reference behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer who submitted none of the sampled filings sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-001 and report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the three computed rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Build the per-jurisdiction earliest-use date register for the Accident launch
actions: Export from the filing tracker every Accident TOI H03 row for the launch with jurisdiction, form numbers and editions, review method and filing status.
For approved rows, set earliest-use date = disposition date, unless the approval letter names a later effective date, in which case take the letter's date.
For file-and-use rows, set earliest-use date = the state's stated post-filing wait; for prior-approval rows with no disposition, leave the date blank and mark the jurisdiction BLOCKED.
Circulate the register to the Insurance Product Manager and Compliance for confirmation before any configuration is dated.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction in the launch carries either a dated earliest-use date with its source, or a BLOCKED flag.

checklist.step: Compute and evidence the deemer satisfaction date where reliance is intended
actions: For each jurisdiction where the launch depends on a deemer, read the statute's review period and the conditions that suspend or extend it.
Take the state's receipt date from the SERFF filing and add the review period - Alaska 30 days from receipt, plus any noticed 30-day extension.
Check the SERFF correspondence thread for any objection, extension notice or request for information that resets or suspends the clock.
Record a written counsel opinion on the tracker row stating the deemer date and that no state action suspended it; no gate opens on deemer without this opinion.
checklist.done: every deemer-based earliest-use date carries a dated counsel opinion confirming the clock ran unsuspended.

checklist.step: Configure state availability so blocked jurisdictions cannot quote or issue
actions: Set the product availability rule for the Accident product by jurisdiction with an available-from date equal to the earliest-use date from the register.
Leave BLOCKED jurisdictions with no available-from date so the product cannot be selected at all, rather than relying on a warning message.
Apply the same date to the form attachment rules so the new edition cannot attach before the earliest-use date.
Screenshot the configuration screen per jurisdiction and attach it to the change record as gate evidence.
checklist.done: policy admin holds a dated availability rule per jurisdiction, blocked states are unselectable and screenshots are attached to the change record.

checklist.step: Mirror the block into rating, quoting and distribution channels
actions: Confirm the broker and agent portal hides the Accident product for blocked jurisdictions and does not allow a saved quote to be converted.
Confirm the rating engine returns no rate for a blocked jurisdiction rather than a zero or default rate.
Confirm the direct customer self-service journey and any call-centre script suppress the product for blocked jurisdictions.
Record each channel check with the date, tester and result on the gate record.
checklist.done: every quoting and distribution channel refuses the product in blocked jurisdictions, with dated evidence per channel.

checklist.step: Prove the block in the test environment before production release
actions: In UAT attempt a new business quote and issue for two blocked jurisdictions and confirm the system refuses at product selection.
Attempt an issue dated one day before the earliest-use date in an approved jurisdiction and confirm it is refused.
Attempt an issue on the earliest-use date and confirm it succeeds and attaches the approved form edition.
Record the three test results with screenshots as the gate's functional evidence and attach them to the release record.
checklist.done: negative and positive gate tests are executed with screenshots showing refusal before the date and success on it.

checklist.step: Require documented approval evidence before any gate is opened
actions: Define the only acceptable evidence: the state's disposition report and approval letter downloaded from SERFF, or the counsel deemer opinion with the SERFF correspondence extract.
Reject as evidence any email summary, verbal confirmation from a state analyst, or a tracker status entered without an attachment.
Attach the evidence to the gate record for the jurisdiction and name the approval date it establishes.
Return any gate request with incomplete evidence to the Regulatory Filing Specialist rather than opening on assurance.
checklist.done: every gate request carries either a downloaded state approval document or a counsel deemer opinion attached to the record.

checklist.step: Apply two-person authorisation to each gate opening
actions: Have the Regulatory Filing Specialist propose the gate opening with the jurisdiction, form editions, approval date and evidence attached.
Have the Compliance Officer independently confirm the approval date from the attached document before authorising.
Record both names, roles and timestamps on the gate record; no single person may propose and authorise.
Only after both signatures are captured may Configuration Engineering set the availability date live.
checklist.done: each opened gate shows two named authorisers with timestamps and the approval evidence they relied on.

checklist.step: Handle partial approvals where only some forms cleared
actions: Read the disposition form list and identify which form numbers and editions were approved and which were not.
Open the gate only for the approved forms and keep the unapproved endorsements or riders unavailable in that jurisdiction.
Check the product's mandatory form set - where a mandatory form is unapproved, the whole jurisdiction stays blocked even if the base policy cleared.
Record the partial position explicitly on the gate record rather than opening the jurisdiction wholesale.
checklist.done: partial approvals are configured form by form and no jurisdiction is opened while a mandatory form remains unapproved.

checklist.step: Apply approval conditions stated in the state's letter
actions: Read each approval letter for conditions - approved for new business only, approved as amended, approved effective a stated date, approved subject to a filed amendment.
Translate each condition into a configuration instruction: new-business-only conditions must block the form on in-force endorsements and renewals.
Where the approval was 'as amended', confirm the amended edition is the one loaded in the forms repository before the gate opens.
Record the condition verbatim on the gate record and name the configuration change that implements it.
checklist.done: every approval condition is transcribed verbatim and mapped to a named configuration change before the gate opens.

checklist.step: Reverse the launch cleanly where a filing is disapproved or withdrawn
actions: On a disapproval or withdrawal, set the jurisdiction back to BLOCKED the same business day and confirm quoting and issue stop across all channels.
Identify any policies already issued on the affected form in that jurisdiction and hand the list to Regulatory Counsel.
Revert the forms repository to the previously approved edition so in-flight business issues on a compliant form.
Record the reversal, its timestamp and the authoriser on the gate record.
checklist.done: the jurisdiction is blocked the same day, the previously approved edition is restored and any issued policies are handed to counsel.

checklist.step: Put the gate on the release readiness agenda as a standing veto
actions: Add the gate register to the release readiness review as a mandatory item with the count of open, blocked and approved jurisdictions.
Require the Compliance Officer's attendance and record a go or no-go per jurisdiction, not a single global go.
Attach the change record's gate evidence to the release ticket so approval cannot be granted without it.
Where any blocked jurisdiction is configured live, hold the release until it is corrected.
checklist.done: the release ticket carries a per-jurisdiction go or no-go decision with the Compliance Officer recorded as present.

checklist.step: Run the day-one issue check after go-live
actions: On the first business day after each gate opens, extract every Accident policy issued by jurisdiction, form number and edition and issue timestamp.
Compare each issue date to the jurisdiction's earliest-use date and confirm no policy pre-dates it.
Confirm the correct approved edition attached by opening two issued policy documents per jurisdiction.
Escalate any pre-date or wrong-edition hit to Compliance within one hour of finding it.
checklist.done: day-one issue data is checked per jurisdiction with no pre-dated policies and the correct edition confirmed on sampled documents.

checklist.step: Run the standing daily open-gate exception report
actions: Schedule a daily report joining live product availability by jurisdiction to the filing tracker's approval status.
Raise an exception for any jurisdiction where the Accident product is available but no approval or satisfied deemer is recorded.
Route exceptions to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Compliance Officer the same morning with the policy count issued since availability opened.
Track each exception to closure - either evidence produced or availability withdrawn.
checklist.done: the daily report runs, exceptions are routed the same morning and each is closed by evidence or by withdrawing availability.

checklist.step: Treat any pre-approval issuance as a breach, not a defect
actions: On any confirmed pre-approval issuance, stop further issuance in that jurisdiction immediately and quantify policies, premium and insureds affected.
Instruct Regulatory Counsel to assess self-reporting to the Division and to advise on remediation for policyholders on the unapproved form.
Open a formal breach record with the root cause, containment action, remediation plan and reporting decision.
Report the breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting regardless of size.
checklist.done: issuance is stopped, exposure is quantified, counsel has advised on self-reporting and a breach record is reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Close and archive the gate record for each jurisdiction
actions: Assemble the gate record per jurisdiction: approval evidence or deemer opinion, earliest-use date and its derivation, two-person authorisation, configuration screenshots, UAT gate test results and day-one issue check.
File it in the compliance evidence repository indexed by jurisdiction, form number, edition and approval date.
Apply the 7-year-from-form-withdrawal retention label so the record survives the product's sunset.
Confirm the record is retrievable by jurisdiction and form number in a search test.
checklist.done: a complete, labelled and retrievable gate record exists in the repository for every jurisdiction in the launch.

testing.step: Build the population of Accident policies issued in the quarter
actions: Extract every Accident policy and certificate issued in the quarter with jurisdiction, writing company, form numbers and editions attached, issue timestamp and effective date.
Include endorsements issued on in-force policies, since a new endorsement edition is itself a pre-use event.
Reconcile the policy count and premium to the finance new-business report for the quarter and clear differences before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extract query and date recorded.
testing.done: the issued-policy population reconciles to the finance new-business report and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the earliest-use date register
actions: Join every issued policy to the gate register on jurisdiction plus form number plus edition.
List any issued form and jurisdiction combination that has no gate register row at all - an unregistered form in use is an automatic breach.
Compare each issue timestamp to the jurisdiction's earliest-use date and compute days before or after.
Produce the exception list of policies issued before the earliest-use date with policy numbers, premium and insured counts.
testing.done: every issued policy is matched to a gate register row and every pre-dated issuance is listed with its exposure.

testing.step: Draw the sample of gate openings and record the selection
actions: Take 100% of gate openings in prior-approval jurisdictions, 100% of openings based on deemer reliance, and the Alaska gate as the representative jurisdiction.
Take 15 further gate openings by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 30 in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool in the workpaper.
Include every partial approval and every reversal in the quarter.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers prior-approval, deemer, partial-approval and reversal gates.

testing.step: Re-derive the earliest-use date for each sampled jurisdiction
actions: Open the SERFF filing for the sampled jurisdiction and read the state receipt date, the disposition status, the disposition date and the approval letter text.
Derive the earliest-use date independently - the disposition date, the later date named in the letter, or the statutory review period from receipt where a deemer applies.
Compare to the register's date and treat any difference of even one day as an exception.
Capture the disposition screen and the approval letter into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled jurisdiction has an independently derived earliest-use date compared to the register, with the state document captured.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer arithmetic on every deemer-based gate
actions: Read the jurisdiction's statutory review period and its suspension and extension provisions as at the filing date.
Recompute receipt date plus review period - for Alaska, receipt plus 30 days, plus any noticed 30-day extension.
Read the SERFF correspondence thread for objections, extension notices or information requests that would suspend the clock before that date.
Treat any gate opened on a suspended or miscomputed clock as a reportable breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every deemer-based gate has a recomputed date supported by an unsuspended correspondence record, or is raised as a breach.

testing.step: Test the two-person authorisation and evidence quality
actions: For each sampled gate, confirm a proposer and a separate authoriser are named with timestamps and that no person occupies both roles.
Open the attached evidence and confirm it is a downloaded state disposition or approval letter, or a dated counsel deemer opinion.
Reject email summaries, screenshots of tracker status or verbal confirmations as evidence and log them as fails.
Confirm the authorisation timestamp pre-dates the configuration change that opened availability.
testing.done: every sampled gate shows segregated two-person authorisation, acceptable state evidence and authorisation before configuration.

testing.step: Re-perform the availability configuration check in the live system
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction, open the product availability rule and read the available-from date and the form attachment effective dates.
Compare both to the independently derived earliest-use date and flag any configuration dated earlier.
Confirm every jurisdiction still marked BLOCKED in the register has no available-from date in the live configuration.
Screenshot each configuration screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: live availability and form attachment dates match the derived earliest-use dates and blocked jurisdictions remain unselectable.

testing.step: Test approval conditions and partial approvals in configuration
actions: For each sampled approval letter carrying a condition, confirm the named configuration change implements it - new-business-only forms blocked on renewals and endorsements.
For partial approvals, confirm unapproved forms are unavailable in that jurisdiction and that no mandatory form is missing from the approved set.
Pull two issued policy documents per condition and confirm the condition holds in the issued output, not only in configuration.
Log any condition recorded but not configured as a fail.
testing.done: every approval condition and partial approval is proved in both configuration and issued policy documents.

testing.step: Log every exception and breach with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise an issue per exception with jurisdiction, form number and edition, policies affected, premium exposure and what failed.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - gate opened on weak evidence, deemer miscomputed, configuration dated early, channel not mirrored, condition not configured - and an owner.
For any pre-approval issuance, open a breach record and a counsel-led self-report assessment for the affected Division.
Set remediation dates and carry every open item into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, and every pre-approval issuance has a breach record and counsel assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the pre-use gate test
actions: Report the count of policies issued before an earliest-use date against the zero-tolerance threshold, with premium and insured exposure.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the workpaper behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who authorised no sampled gate and sits outside Product Operations, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-001 and report every breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the pre-use breach count, exposure, conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.
