checklist.step: Turn each approval letter into a configuration specification
actions: Read the disposition letter and the approved Form Schedule and list each approved form number, edition date, form type and jurisdiction.
Write the specification row by row: which form attaches, in which jurisdiction, for which product and coverage combination, from which effective date, mandatory or optional.
Add the conditions from the approval letter - new business only, approved as amended, stated effective date - as explicit configuration requirements.
Have the Product Filing Specialist confirm the specification matches the determination and disposition before development starts.
checklist.done: a specification exists naming every approved form, jurisdiction, attachment condition and effective date, confirmed by Product Compliance.

checklist.step: Raise the change record and link it to the filing evidence
actions: Raise a change record naming the Accident product, the jurisdictions in scope, the form editions and the target activation dates.
Attach the SERFF tracking numbers, disposition letters and the configuration specification to the change record.
Set the change's implementation window so production verification completes before the earliest jurisdiction's earliest-use date.
Add the Compliance Officer as a required approver so the change cannot progress without compliance review.
checklist.done: the change record carries the filing evidence, the specification, a dated window and Compliance as a required approver.

checklist.step: Load the approved form PDFs and templates into the document library
actions: Download the approved form attachments from the SERFF disposition, not from the internal draft folder, so the loaded file is the file the state holds.
Load each into the document generation template library named <form number>_<edition>_<state> and record the checksum.
Compare the loaded checksum to the SERFF-downloaded file checksum and reject any mismatch.
Mark the superseded edition as retired with an end date equal to the new edition's effective date in that jurisdiction.
checklist.done: every approved edition is loaded from the SERFF copy with a matching checksum and the superseded edition is dated out.

checklist.step: Configure form availability and attachment rules by jurisdiction
actions: Create the form availability rows for the Accident product by jurisdiction with the effective-from date set to the earliest-use date from the gate register.
Configure the attachment logic - base policy plus mandatory notices, state-mandated endorsements and the outline of coverage where the jurisdiction requires it at delivery.
Configure optional riders to attach only when the corresponding coverage is selected, and only in jurisdictions where the rider was approved.
Configure state-variant forms to supersede the countrywide form in their jurisdiction so both can never attach to the same policy.
checklist.done: availability and attachment rules are configured per jurisdiction with correct mandatory, optional and state-variant behaviour.

checklist.step: Load the approved rate tables and factors into the rating engine
actions: Take the rate tables from the filed rate exhibit attached to the SERFF Rate/Rule Schedule, not from the pricing working file.
Load base rates, issue-age factors, benefit-amount relativities, occupational class factors and any policy fee, effective-dated to the jurisdiction's earliest-use date.
Configure minimum and maximum benefit amounts and issue ages exactly as filed so an out-of-range quote is refused rather than rated.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary review the loaded tables against the filed exhibit cell by cell and initial the review.
checklist.done: rate tables and limits are loaded from the filed exhibit, effective-dated, and cell-verified by the filing actuary.

checklist.step: Configure the state-specific mandated content
actions: Configure the jurisdiction-specific free-look period, grace period and cancellation notice periods as filed for each jurisdiction.
Configure the fraud warning wording per jurisdiction on applications and claim forms, using the exact filed text.
Configure guaranty association and grievance notices to attach at delivery where the jurisdiction requires them.
Record each configured value against the filed source page so the mapping can be re-tested.
checklist.done: every state-mandated period, warning and notice is configured to its filed value with the source page recorded.

checklist.step: Run the developer unit test on quote and issue in each jurisdiction
actions: In the development environment quote and issue one Accident policy per jurisdiction in scope at a standard issue age and benefit amount.
Confirm the produced form packet lists exactly the forms the specification requires, with the approved edition dates in the footers.
Confirm the quote refuses out-of-range benefit amounts and issue ages as filed.
Log any missing, extra or wrong-edition form as a defect against the change record before UAT starts.
checklist.done: each jurisdiction produces the specified form packet at the approved editions in development, with defects logged and cleared.

checklist.step: Compare the generated document to the SERFF-filed PDF page by page
actions: Generate a full policy document from the test policy and place it side by side with the SERFF-filed PDF for the same form number and edition.
Run an automated text diff and then read the schedule page, benefit definitions, exclusions and termination provisions by eye.
Confirm every bracketed value in the issued document sits inside the range stated in the filed Statement of Variability.
Record the diff result and the reviewer's name and date; a clean diff is the only pass condition.
checklist.done: a documented page-by-page comparison shows the issued document identical to the filed edition, with brackets inside filed ranges.

checklist.step: Reproduce filed premiums from the loaded rate tables
actions: Take the worked premium examples from the filed actuarial memorandum for at least three issue ages and two benefit amounts per rate structure.
Quote the same scenarios in the rating engine and compare the resulting premium to the filed example to the cent.
Investigate every difference beyond rounding as a loading error rather than accepting a tolerance.
Sign the reproduction worksheet and attach it to the change record.
checklist.done: quoted premiums reproduce the filed worked examples to the cent for every tested scenario, with a signed worksheet attached.

checklist.step: Regression test in-force endorsement, renewal and reinstatement paths
actions: Endorse an in-force Accident policy written on the prior edition and confirm the endorsement attaches the correct edition for that policy's original form set.
Renew a policy across the new edition's effective date and confirm the renewal follows the approval condition - prior edition where the approval is new business only.
Reinstate a lapsed policy and confirm the reinstated contract keeps its original filed edition.
Log every case where the new edition attaches to business the approval did not cover.
checklist.done: endorsement, renewal and reinstatement paths attach the edition the approval permits, with any mis-attachment logged as a defect.

checklist.step: Obtain UAT sign-off from Product and Compliance
actions: Run the UAT script covering quote, issue, document output, premium reproduction, mandated content and the endorsement and renewal paths, per jurisdiction.
Have the Insurance Product Manager sign the product behaviour and the Compliance Officer sign the form fidelity and mandated content.
Record every UAT defect with severity; no severity 1 or 2 defect may remain open at sign-off.
Attach the signed UAT pack to the change record.
checklist.done: a signed UAT pack with zero open severity 1 or 2 defects is attached to the change record.

checklist.step: Deploy through change control with effective dating, not switch-on
actions: Obtain change approval from the Head of IT and the Compliance Officer with the UAT pack and gate evidence attached.
Deploy the configuration with effective dates set per jurisdiction so activation happens on the earliest-use date rather than on deployment day.
Confirm the deployment log records the template versions and checksums promoted to production.
Keep a documented rollback plan naming the prior template versions and rate table versions.
checklist.done: the change is approved, deployed with per-jurisdiction effective dating, checksum-logged and covered by a rollback plan.

checklist.step: Verify in production with a controlled test policy
actions: On the activation date, issue a controlled test policy in production for two jurisdictions and generate the full document packet.
Compare the production document to the SERFF-filed PDF and the production premium to the filed worked example.
Confirm the production template checksums match the checksums recorded at load from SERFF.
Cancel the test policies flat and record the verification result and timestamps on the change record.
checklist.done: production output matches the filed form and premium, checksums match, and the test policies are cancelled flat with evidence recorded.

checklist.step: Retire superseded editions and update the forms inventory
actions: Set the end date on the superseded edition in the forms inventory to the day before the new edition's effective date in each jurisdiction.
Confirm the superseded template cannot be selected for new business while remaining available for in-force servicing of policies issued on it.
Update the inventory with the new edition's SERFF tracking number, approval date and jurisdictions approved.
Circulate the updated inventory to Underwriting, Claims and the contact centre so no one issues from a stale library copy.
checklist.done: the inventory shows dated supersession, the SERFF reference on the new edition, and distribution of the update to servicing teams.

checklist.step: Close the change record and file the implementation evidence
actions: Assemble the evidence pack: specification, disposition letters, template checksums, diff result, rate reproduction worksheet, UAT sign-off, deployment log and production verification.
File it in the compliance evidence repository indexed by jurisdiction, form number, edition and SERFF tracking number.
Close the change record with a link to the evidence pack and the activation timestamps per jurisdiction.
Apply the 7-year-from-form-withdrawal retention label.
checklist.done: a complete, indexed and retention-labelled implementation evidence pack exists and the change record is closed against it.

testing.step: Build the population of Accident configuration changes deployed in the quarter
actions: Extract every change record touching Accident forms, templates, attachment rules or rate tables with a deployment date inside the quarter.
Add the document library version history and the rating engine table version history so a template or table changed outside change control is exposed.
Reconcile the change records to the deployment logs and list every deployed version with no approved change record.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and criteria recorded.
testing.done: deployed template and rate versions reconcile to approved change records and the population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile deployed form editions to approved SERFF dispositions
actions: Join each deployed form edition and jurisdiction to a SERFF disposition showing that edition approved for that jurisdiction.
List any edition live in production with no approval for that jurisdiction as an automatic breach and quantify the policies issued on it.
Confirm the deployment effective date is on or after the disposition date recorded in SERFF.
Capture the disposition list used for the reconciliation into the workpaper.
testing.done: every deployed edition traces to an approval for its jurisdiction and any unapproved live edition is quantified as a breach.

testing.step: Draw the sample of changes and issued documents
actions: Take 100% of changes affecting prior-approval jurisdictions and 100% of changes affecting Alaska as the representative jurisdiction.
Take 15 further changes by seeded random selection and, for each sampled change, draw 3 issued policy documents from production.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool in the workpaper.
Include at least one endorsement-path and one renewal-path document in the document sample.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers prior-approval and Alaska changes and includes endorsement and renewal documents.

testing.step: Re-perform the document diff against the SERFF-filed PDF
actions: Download the approved form PDF directly from the SERFF disposition rather than from the internal repository.
Run an independent text diff against each sampled issued policy document and read the schedule page, exclusions and termination provisions by eye.
Treat every wording difference as a fail, including punctuation and defined-term capitalisation, and record the page and line.
Capture the diff output and both source documents into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled document has an independent diff against the SERFF-downloaded PDF with every difference recorded.

testing.step: Verify template checksums between SERFF, the library and production
actions: Compute the checksum of the SERFF-downloaded PDF for each sampled form edition.
Compare it to the checksum recorded at load in the template library and to the checksum of the template deployed in production.
Flag any three-way mismatch and identify which version the issued documents actually used.
Read the library version history for any edit made after the load date and check whether it went through change control.
testing.done: checksums agree across SERFF, library and production for every sampled edition, or the mismatch and its source are identified.

testing.step: Independently reproduce premiums from the filed rate exhibits
actions: Take the filed rate tables from the SERFF Rate/Rule Schedule for each sampled jurisdiction.
Recompute the premium for five issued policies drawn from production using their actual issue age, benefit amount and occupational class.
Compare the recomputed premium to the premium charged on the policy to the cent and list every difference.
Check that policies outside the filed issue-age or benefit-amount limits were not issued at all.
testing.done: charged premiums reproduce from the filed tables to the cent for every recomputed policy and no out-of-limit policy exists.

testing.step: Test attachment rules, state variants and mandated content on issued policies
actions: For each sampled issued policy, list the forms attached and compare to the specification's mandatory and optional set for that jurisdiction.
Confirm the state-variant form attached where one exists and that the countrywide form did not attach alongside it.
Check the free-look period, grace period and fraud warning printed on the document against the filed values for that jurisdiction.
Log missing mandatory forms and wrong mandated values separately, since a missing mandated notice is a market conduct finding in its own right.
testing.done: attached form sets, state variants and mandated values match the filed position on every sampled policy, or are logged.

testing.step: Test the change-control discipline behind each sampled deployment
actions: Confirm each sampled change record carries the disposition letters, the specification, the signed UAT pack and Compliance approval before deployment.
Confirm no severity 1 or 2 UAT defect was open at sign-off and that the sign-off pre-dates the deployment timestamp.
Confirm the deployment used per-jurisdiction effective dating rather than an immediate switch-on, and that the rollback plan names prior versions.
Flag any emergency change that bypassed the output-versus-filed comparison.
testing.done: each sampled deployment shows complete pre-approval evidence, clean UAT, effective dating and no bypassed fidelity comparison.

testing.step: Log defects and breaches with root cause, owner and correction plan
actions: Raise a defect per finding with jurisdiction, form number and edition, the affected policy count and the wording or premium difference described precisely.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - template loaded from draft, rate table transcribed by hand, attachment rule wrong, mandated value stale, change bypassed - and an owner.
For issued documents that differ from the filed form, agree with Regulatory Counsel whether policyholder correction and Division notification are required.
Set correction dates and carry every open defect into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every defect has an owner, root cause, correction date and, where documents differ from the filed form, a counsel decision on remediation.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the implementation fidelity test
actions: Report the count of documents differing from the filed edition and the count of premiums differing from the filed tables against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, with workpaper references behind each count.
Have the independent reviewer, who configured and signed no sampled change, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-001 and report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with document and premium difference counts, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Detect the objection letter on the day the state issues it
actions: Run the daily SERFF workspace sweep filtered to Accident TOI H03 filings and check the message centre and the Objection Letters tab on each open filing.
Confirm SERFF email notifications route to a monitored team address as well as the named filing contact, so a single person's absence cannot hide a letter.
Open each new objection letter, download it and save it to the filing folder as <state>-objection-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf.
Record the receipt date and the reviewer's name and contact details on the objection log the same day.
checklist.done: every objection letter is downloaded and logged with its receipt date on the day it appears in SERFF.

checklist.step: Capture the state's stated response due date and arm the clock
actions: Read the objection letter for the response deadline the state states - commonly 10 to 30 days - and copy it verbatim into the tracker row.
Where the letter states no deadline, apply the house standard of 10 business days from receipt and note that the date is internal, not statutory.
Record whether the letter says the review clock is suspended until a response is filed, since that resets the deemer date computed at submission.
Set alerts at due date minus 5 and minus 2 business days and an escalation alert to the Compliance Manager on the due date.
checklist.done: the tracker holds the stated due date, its source, the clock-suspension position and three armed alerts.

checklist.step: Triage the objection into typed items with named owners
actions: Split the letter into numbered objection items - one row per point the reviewer raises, even where the letter runs them together in a paragraph.
Type each item: form wording, mandated content omission, readability, variability, actuarial or rate, filing mechanics, or state interpretation.
Assign each item an owner - Policy Forms Specialist for wording, Product / Filing Actuary for rate and memorandum items, Regulatory Counsel for interpretation, the filing analyst for mechanics.
Set an internal due date for each item at least 3 business days before the state's stated due date.
checklist.done: every objection point is a typed, owned row with an internal due date ahead of the state's deadline.

checklist.step: Read the requirement the reviewer is actually citing
actions: For each objection item, open the statute, regulation, bulletin or checklist item the letter cites and read it in full.
Compare the cited requirement to the as-filed document and decide whether the objection is well founded, partly founded, or based on a misreading of the filing.
Where the reviewer cites nothing, look the requirement up in the state's current SERFF filing rules for TOI H03 and record what was found.
Write a short position note per item stating the requirement, the current filed position and the gap.
checklist.done: each objection item has a position note naming the requirement text, the filed position and the gap.

checklist.step: Draft the substantive response for each item
actions: Answer each numbered item separately, restating the reviewer's point before the answer so the letter can be read alone.
Where the objection is accepted, state the amendment made and identify the revised form number, edition date and page.
Where the objection is not accepted, cite the statute, bulletin or prior approval relied upon and attach the supporting document.
Never answer an item with a bare assertion of compliance - point to the text that satisfies the requirement.
checklist.done: every numbered item has a self-contained answer that either identifies the amendment or cites the authority relied upon.

checklist.step: Amend the forms and re-version the edition where the objection is accepted
actions: Make the wording change in the source document and advance the edition date per the house convention so the amended form is distinguishable from the as-filed version.
Regenerate the filing-grade PDF, confirm the new edition date prints in the footer of every page, and lock the version.
Update the redline so it shows the change against both the previously approved edition and the version originally filed in this submission.
Notify the Business Systems Analyst that the edition destined for configuration has changed, before implementation starts on the wrong version.
checklist.done: amended forms carry a new edition date in the footer, a two-way redline and a notification to the implementation team.

checklist.step: Refresh the actuarial memorandum and rate exhibits where the objection is actuarial
actions: Answer rate and loss-ratio objections with the recomputed demonstration rather than a narrative explanation.
Where an assumption is changed, reissue the memorandum with a new date, restate the anticipated lifetime loss ratio and re-sign the certification.
Update the worked premium examples so they still reproduce from the attached rate tables after any change.
Confirm the overall rate impact fields in the SERFF Rate/Rule Schedule still match the revised memorandum.
checklist.done: actuarial items are answered with a re-signed memorandum whose loss ratio, rate tables and SERFF impact fields reconcile.

checklist.step: Update the Statement of Variability and certifications affected by the amendment
actions: Where amended wording adds, removes or changes a bracket, update the Statement of Variability row and its stated range.
Re-run the readability score on the amended text and reissue the certification where the score or the form edition has changed.
Re-check the amended text against the jurisdiction's mandated content list to confirm the amendment has not broken another requirement.
Reissue any certification that names a form edition that no longer exists.
checklist.done: variability, readability and mandated-content documents are reissued to match the amended edition.

checklist.step: Request an extension in writing before the stated date where more time is needed
actions: Decide at due date minus 5 business days whether the response can be complete on time; do not decide on the due date.
Send the extension request through the SERFF message centre naming the tracking number, the items outstanding, the reason and a specific new date proposed.
Record the request date, the state's reply and any new date granted on the tracker row, and re-arm the alerts to the new date.
Escalate to the Compliance Manager where the state refuses or does not reply before the original due date.
checklist.done: any extension is requested before the original due date, with the state's reply and any new date recorded on the tracker.

checklist.step: Obtain legal clearance on positions and concessions
actions: Review every response that declines an objection, relies on a statutory interpretation, or cites a prior approval as precedent.
Review any response that concedes a defect in a form already in use elsewhere, since the concession may implicate other jurisdictions.
Confirm the response does not commit the company to a practice it cannot administer, such as a variability range outside the system's configuration.
Record the clearance with counsel name and date on the objection log row before submission.
checklist.done: every declining, interpretive or conceding response carries a dated counsel clearance before it is submitted.

checklist.step: Submit the response in SERFF with the amended attachments
actions: Open the filing's Objection Letters tab and use Respond to Objection Letter, answering each numbered item in the response text.
Replace the superseded attachments on the Form Schedule and Supporting Documentation tabs with the amended versions, keeping the original attachment history intact.
Confirm every amended attachment opens and shows the new edition date before submitting the response.
Submit and download the response confirmation with its timestamp into the filing folder.
checklist.done: the response is submitted item by item with amended attachments in place and a timestamped confirmation filed.

checklist.step: Confirm the objection is closed and the review clock has restarted
actions: Watch the filing status after the response and record when the objection moves to closed or a further objection is issued.
Recompute the deemer date from the response date where the state suspended the clock, and update the tracker and the gate register.
Notify the Insurance Product Manager of the revised earliest-use date so the launch plan reflects the slip.
Where a second objection repeats the first, escalate to the Compliance Manager rather than answering the same way twice.
checklist.done: the objection status, recomputed deemer date and revised earliest-use date are recorded and communicated.

checklist.step: Escalate objections approaching or past their due date
actions: Run the weekly open-objection aging report showing days to due date, owner and outstanding items by jurisdiction.
Chase every item still open at due date minus 2 business days directly with its named owner and record the contact.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance any objection that passes its due date unanswered, with the launch impact and the risk of disapproval stated.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether to withdraw and refile rather than let a filing lapse to disapproval.
checklist.done: every objection nearing or past its due date has a logged chase, an escalation and a documented withdraw-or-answer decision.

checklist.step: Handle disapproval and preserve the company's hearing rights
actions: On a disapproval, read the letter for the grounds cited and for the time limit to request a hearing or reconsideration.
Diarise that limit immediately and decide with the Head of Compliance whether to request a hearing, amend and refile, or drop the jurisdiction.
Confirm the jurisdiction's gate is set back to BLOCKED and that no Accident coverage is being issued on the disapproved form.
Record the grounds, the decision and its author on the objection log and in the breach or issue record.
checklist.done: the disapproval grounds, the hearing deadline and the documented decision are recorded and the jurisdiction is blocked.

checklist.step: Feed recurring objections back into the filing package matrix
actions: Each quarter group closed objections by type and jurisdiction and identify defects raised on more than one filing.
For each recurring defect, add or amend the companion-item matrix row and the QC checklist so the next package prevents it.
Publish the top recurring objections to Product Development, Pricing and Legal with the exact state wording that triggered them.
Track each matrix change to completion with an owner and date, and re-measure the repeat rate next quarter.
checklist.done: recurring objections are quantified, converted into owned matrix and QC changes, and re-measured the following quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of objections received in the quarter
actions: Export from SERFF every objection letter issued on Accident TOI H03 filings for the writing companies within the quarter, with jurisdiction, tracking number and issue date.
Export the internal objection log for the same period and reconcile the two on tracking number and objection date.
List every SERFF objection with no internal log row - an undetected objection is the highest-severity finding in this control.
Sign the reconciled population as complete with the export criteria and date.
testing.done: the SERFF objection export and internal log reconcile and every undetected objection is listed.

testing.step: Recompute each response due date from the state's own letter
actions: Open each objection letter and read the stated response deadline and its basis - calendar or business days from issue or from receipt.
Recompute the due date independently and compare it to the date recorded on the tracker row.
Flag every row where the tracker date is later than the recomputed date, since that error alone creates late responses.
Where no deadline was stated, confirm the house 10-business-day standard was applied from the correct receipt date.
testing.done: each objection has an independently recomputed due date compared against the tracker, with every difference flagged.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the selection
actions: Take 100% of objections in prior-approval jurisdictions, 100% of Alaska objections and 100% of objections answered late or unanswered.
Take 15 further objections by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 30 in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool in the workpaper.
Include every objection that led to a disapproval, withdrawal or a second objection on the same point.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers prior-approval, Alaska, late, adverse-outcome and repeat objections.

testing.step: Test response timeliness against the recomputed due dates
actions: Read the response submission timestamp from the SERFF correspondence thread for each sampled objection.
Compute days early or late against the recomputed due date and list every late response as a fail.
Where an extension was granted, confirm the request was sent before the original due date and that the state's grant is in the thread.
Capture the correspondence thread screen showing the objection and response timestamps into the workpaper.
testing.done: days early or late is computed for every sampled objection and every late response and late extension request is listed as a fail.

testing.step: Re-perform the completeness of the response against each numbered objection item
actions: Number the items in the objection letter independently and compare the count to the items answered in the response.
Confirm each answer either identifies the amendment made with form number, edition and page, or cites the authority relied on with an attachment.
Flag answers that assert compliance without pointing to text, since those generate the second objection.
Check whether a second objection on the same filing repeats an item that was answered incompletely.
testing.done: every objection item traces to a substantive answer, with incomplete answers and their downstream second objections flagged.

testing.step: Trace amendments through to the attachments actually on file in SERFF
actions: For each accepted objection, download the current attachment from the Form Schedule and confirm the amended wording is present at the page cited.
Confirm the edition date advanced and that the footer edition matches the transmittal and the Statement of Variability.
Confirm the reissued readability certification and actuarial memorandum, where affected, carry the amended edition and a signature date after the amendment.
Flag any response claiming an amendment that the attachment does not contain.
testing.done: every claimed amendment is present in the SERFF attachment at the cited page with a consistent edition date and reissued certifications.

testing.step: Verify the implementation team received the amended edition
actions: For each amended form, check the template library holds the amended edition and not the version originally filed.
Compare the library checksum to the SERFF-downloaded amended attachment.
Confirm the notification to the Business Systems Analyst exists and pre-dates the configuration change that loaded the template.
Flag any case where the originally filed version reached production.
testing.done: the amended edition is the version held in the library and reached production, with the notification evidenced before configuration.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer impact of clock suspension
actions: For each sampled objection, read whether the letter or the statute suspends the review clock pending a response.
Recompute the deemer date from the response submission date where suspension applies - for Alaska, the remaining balance of the 30-day review runs from the response.
Compare to the earliest-use date used by the gate register and flag any jurisdiction opened on a pre-suspension deemer date.
Treat coverage issued on a stale deemer date as a reportable breach.
testing.done: deemer dates are recomputed for every suspended clock and every gate opened on a stale date is raised as a breach.

testing.step: Log exceptions and quantify the repeat-defect rate
actions: Raise an issue per exception with jurisdiction, tracking number, objection item and what failed - late, incomplete, uncleared, unlogged.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - objection not detected, due date miscaptured, owner unassigned, amendment not attached, no legal clearance - and an owner.
Group closed objections by defect type and compute the repeat-defect rate against the 10% matrix-rebuild trigger.
Set remediation dates and carry every open item into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date, and the repeat-defect rate is computed against the rebuild trigger.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the objection response test
actions: Report the late-response count against the zero-tolerance threshold, the undetected-objection count and the repeat-defect rate.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, with the workpaper reference behind each measure.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted and submitted no sampled response, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-001 and report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the late, undetected and repeat measures, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Define the record set that must exist for every Accident filing
actions: Write the mandatory record list: determination worksheet and dated filing-rules captures, frozen package and manifest, transmittal, as-filed form PDFs, objection letters and responses, disposition report, approval letter and the gate record.
State for each item its source system and the file naming convention <state>-<form number>-<edition>-<document type>.
State that the as-filed PDFs are taken from SERFF, not from the internal drafting folder, so the archived copy is what the state holds.
Publish the list to Product Compliance and the filing analysts as the archive acceptance standard.
checklist.done: a published record list names every mandatory item, its source system and its naming convention.

checklist.step: Export the complete SERFF filing at disposition
actions: Within 10 business days of disposition, open the filing and export the Filing at a Glance and the full filing PDF including schedules, attachments and correspondence.
Download the disposition report, the approval letter and every objection letter and response separately so each is individually retrievable.
Confirm the export includes every attachment version, not only the current one, so the amendment history survives.
Save the export set into the filing folder and record the export date and the exporter.
checklist.done: the complete SERFF export with attachment history and separately saved decision documents sits in the filing folder.

checklist.step: Archive the record set with the full metadata schema
actions: Load the record set into the repository under REG-001 with metadata: jurisdiction, writing company and NAIC code, TOI and Sub-TOI, form number, edition date, SERFF tracking number, submission date, disposition date and status.
Add the earliest-use date and any approval condition so the archive answers the pre-use question without opening the PDFs.
Run the repository's mandatory-metadata validation and clear every blank before the record is accepted.
Link the archived record back to the filing tracker row and the change record that implemented it.
checklist.done: the record is loaded with complete metadata, validated for blanks and linked to the tracker and change record.

checklist.step: Apply the retention label keyed to form withdrawal, not filing date
actions: Apply the retention rule of 7 years from withdrawal of the form edition, and set the trigger field to the edition's withdrawal date rather than a fixed date.
Where a jurisdiction's own retention or examination lookback is longer, apply the longer period and record which jurisdiction drove it.
Leave the withdrawal date open while the edition remains in use so the clock cannot start early.
Confirm the applied label on a sample record by reading the repository's computed disposal date.
checklist.done: each record carries a withdrawal-triggered retention label, the longest applicable period, and a verifiable computed disposal date.

checklist.step: Register the approved edition in the controlled forms inventory
actions: Add the approved edition to the forms inventory with its jurisdictions approved, SERFF tracking numbers, approval dates and earliest-use dates.
Attach the SERFF-sourced PDF as the controlled copy and mark the internal drafting version as non-authoritative.
Record the supersession chain so any edition can be traced back through its predecessors to the original approval.
Set the edition's withdrawal date when it is retired, which starts the retention clock in the archive.
checklist.done: the inventory holds the SERFF-sourced controlled copy, the approval references and a complete supersession chain.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive index to the filing tracker monthly
actions: Extract every filing dispositioned in the month from the tracker and every record archived in the month from the repository.
Match on SERFF tracking number and list dispositioned filings with no archived record and archived records with no tracker row.
Chase each unarchived disposition with the responsible filing analyst and record the date archived.
Report the monthly unarchived count and aging to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the monthly reconciliation is run, every unarchived disposition is chased to closure and the count is reported.

checklist.step: Control access to the archive and keep the record immutable
actions: Grant read access to Product Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit and the examination response team, and write access only to Compliance Ops.
Set archived records to read-only on acceptance so an as-filed PDF cannot be replaced with a later version.
Enable the repository audit trail on view, download and delete events and confirm events are retained for the life of the record.
Recertify access to the REG-001 archive at each quarterly user access review.
checklist.done: archived records are read-only, access is role-limited and recertified quarterly, and the audit trail captures downloads and deletions.

checklist.step: Apply legal hold when an examination, complaint or litigation touches a filing
actions: On notice of a market conduct examination, Division inquiry, complaint or litigation, identify the affected jurisdictions, form numbers and editions.
Apply a legal hold flag to the matching archive records so retention-based disposal cannot run on them.
Notify the Records Manager and Compliance Ops of the hold scope and its start date in writing.
Release the hold only in writing when the matter closes, and record the release date on each record.
checklist.done: affected records carry a dated legal hold that overrides disposal, with a written scope and a documented release.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly market conduct retrieval drill
actions: Pick two jurisdictions at random, one of them a prior-approval state, and simulate an examiner request for all Accident forms in use in a stated period.
Assemble the packet from the archive alone: as-filed forms, approval letters, correspondence, earliest-use dates and the form list in force in the period.
Time the assembly from request to complete packet and compare it to the 5-business-day standard.
Log every record that could not be found or was incomplete, and reconstruct it from SERFF the same week.
checklist.done: the drill packet is assembled from the archive within 5 business days with every gap logged and reconstructed.

checklist.step: Reconstruct missing records from the regulator's own copy
actions: For each missing record, search SERFF Filing Access by NAIC company code, jurisdiction, TOI H03 and form number to locate the filing.
Re-export the filing, disposition report and approval letter and archive them with a note recording that the record was reconstructed and when.
Where SERFF no longer holds the filing, request a certified copy from the Division and record the request and response.
Raise an issue for every reconstruction so the archiving gap is root-caused rather than quietly fixed.
checklist.done: every missing record is reconstructed from SERFF or the Division, annotated as reconstructed, and root-caused in an issue.

checklist.step: Migrate legacy Accident filing records into the same index
actions: Inventory Accident filing records held in shared drives, email archives or a predecessor system for editions still inside the retention window.
Load them into the repository under the same metadata schema, filling jurisdiction, form number, edition and SERFF tracking number from the documents themselves.
Where a legacy record lacks the SERFF tracking number, retrieve it from SERFF Filing Access rather than leaving the field blank.
Decommission the legacy location only after a reconciliation shows every in-scope record migrated.
checklist.done: in-scope legacy records are migrated under the standard schema and the legacy location is decommissioned only after reconciliation.

checklist.step: Hold third-party filer and vendor records to the same standard
actions: Where a third-party filer submits Accident filings, require delivery of the full SERFF export and correspondence within 10 business days of disposition.
Write the retention, retrieval and return-on-termination obligations into the vendor contract and check them at each contract review.
Reconcile vendor-filed dispositions to the archive monthly, since a vendor-held record is not a compliant record.
Obtain an annual attestation from the vendor that no company filing record has been destroyed.
checklist.done: vendor-filed records reach the archive within 10 business days, with contractual retention terms and an annual destruction attestation.

checklist.step: Test backup and restore of the archive
actions: Confirm the repository is inside the backup scope with a recovery point objective consistent with a 7-year record set.
Restore a sample of five archived Accident filing records into an isolated environment at least annually.
Open the restored PDFs and confirm they are readable and that the metadata restored with them.
Record the restore test date, records tested and result, and raise an issue on any unreadable or metadata-less restore.
checklist.done: an annual restore test shows sampled archived records recoverable, readable and complete with metadata.

checklist.step: Dispose of records only after the retention period and with authorisation
actions: Run the annual disposal sweep listing records whose 7-year clock from form withdrawal has expired.
Exclude every record under legal hold and every record where a longer jurisdiction-specific period applies.
Obtain written authorisation from the Head of Compliance and Legal Counsel before any deletion, and record the authorisation against each record.
Keep a permanent disposal certificate listing what was destroyed, when, under what authority and by whom.
checklist.done: disposal runs only on expired, unheld records with written authorisation and a permanent disposal certificate.

checklist.step: Attest the archive annually against the filing inventory
actions: Receive the annual archive report showing dispositioned filings, archived records, unarchived exceptions, holds and disposals for the Accident portfolio.
Confirm every form edition currently in use in any of the 51 jurisdictions has a complete archived record behind it.
Sign the attestation and record any qualification, naming the jurisdictions and editions affected.
Report the attestation and any qualification to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation exists confirming complete archived records behind every in-use edition, with qualifications named.

testing.step: Build the population of Accident filings inside the retention window
actions: Extract every Accident TOI H03 filing dispositioned within the retention window from the filing tracker, with jurisdiction, tracking number, form numbers and editions.
Add every Accident form edition in the controlled forms inventory whose withdrawal date is less than seven years ago or is still open.
Reconcile both lists to a SERFF Filing Access search by NAIC company code and TOI H03 to catch filings absent from internal systems.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and criteria recorded.
testing.done: the population reconciles across tracker, forms inventory and SERFF and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the archive index
actions: Join every population row to an archive index entry on SERFF tracking number plus form number plus edition.
List every dispositioned filing and every in-use edition with no archived record as an automatic fail.
Check the archive-date field against the disposition date and compute the days taken against the 10-business-day standard.
Quantify the exposure - jurisdictions where an in-use form has no archived approval evidence.
testing.done: every filing and in-use edition is matched to an archived record or listed as a fail, with archiving latency computed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the selection
actions: Take 100% of prior-approval jurisdictions' records for editions currently in use, plus all Alaska records as the representative jurisdiction.
Take 20 further records by seeded random selection across the retention window, weighted to the oldest years, minimum 40 in total.
Record seed, population size, selection date and tool in the workpaper.
Include at least five legacy-migrated records and any vendor-filed records.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers prior-approval, Alaska, oldest-year, legacy-migrated and vendor-filed records.

testing.step: Test each sampled record against the mandatory record list
actions: Open each sampled archive record and tick each mandatory item - determination worksheet, rules captures, frozen package and manifest, transmittal, as-filed PDFs, objections and responses, disposition report, approval letter, gate record.
Confirm the metadata fields are populated and correct, especially jurisdiction, edition date, tracking number and earliest-use date.
Open two PDFs per record and confirm they are readable, complete and carry the printed edition date.
Log any record missing an item as incomplete rather than partially compliant.
testing.done: each sampled record is scored against the mandatory list with missing items logged and file readability confirmed.

testing.step: Verify the archived as-filed PDF against the regulator's copy
actions: For each sampled record, download the approved form attachment directly from SERFF Filing Access.
Compare it to the archived copy by checksum and, where checksums differ, by page-by-page diff.
Flag any archived copy that is the internal draft rather than the SERFF-sourced version, since only the latter proves what the state approved.
Capture both files and the comparison result into the workpaper.
testing.done: archived as-filed PDFs match the SERFF copy by checksum or diff, and every internally sourced substitute is flagged.

testing.step: Recompute the retention clock on each sampled record
actions: Read the form edition's withdrawal date from the controlled forms inventory, or confirm it is still open where the edition remains in use.
Recompute the disposal date as withdrawal plus seven years, or the longer jurisdiction-specific period where one applies.
Compare to the repository's computed disposal date and flag any record whose clock was started from the filing date instead of withdrawal.
Flag any record with an open withdrawal date that nonetheless shows a scheduled disposal date.
testing.done: recomputed disposal dates match the repository for every sampled record, or the miscalculated clock is flagged.

testing.step: Test legal holds, access controls and immutability
actions: List open examinations, complaints and litigation touching Accident forms and confirm a dated legal hold exists on every matching archive record.
Pull the repository access list for the REG-001 archive and confirm write access is limited to Compliance Ops and was recertified in the last quarter.
Attempt a controlled overwrite of a test archived record and confirm the repository refuses it.
Read the audit trail for delete events inside the retention window and investigate every one.
testing.done: every open matter has a dated hold, write access is limited and recertified, overwrite is refused and deletions are investigated.

testing.step: Re-perform the market conduct retrieval drill independently
actions: Issue an unannounced request in the examiner's own terms - every Accident form in use in one prior-approval jurisdiction and in Alaska over a stated 12-month period, with approvals.
Time the assembly of the packet from the archive alone, without going to SERFF or to the filing analysts.
Check the packet answers the examiner's real question: which forms were in use, on what authority, from what date.
Compare the elapsed time to the 5-business-day standard and record every gap that had to be filled from outside the archive.
testing.done: the drill packet is produced from the archive alone within 5 business days or the shortfall and its gaps are recorded.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and reconstruction plan
actions: Raise an issue per exception with jurisdiction, form number and edition, tracking number and the specific record item missing or wrong.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list - disposition not archived, internal draft archived instead of SERFF copy, metadata blank, clock started from filing date, hold not applied, vendor record not delivered - and an owner.
Require reconstruction from SERFF or the Division within 20 business days and record the reconstruction date.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance any record that cannot be reconstructed at all, with the examination exposure stated.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and reconstruction date, and unreconstructable records are escalated with exposure stated.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the archive and retention test
actions: Report the count of dispositioned filings and in-use editions with no complete archived record, against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Report the archiving latency distribution against the 10-business-day standard and the retrieval drill elapsed time against the 5-business-day standard.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the workpaper behind each measure.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Compliance Ops and archived no sampled record, sign the workpaper, then file it under REG-001 and report to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with completeness, latency and retrieval measures, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.
